newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria cbank cuts main interest rate to 5.42 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria cbank cuts main interest rate to 5.42 pct.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) cut its main lev interest rate to 5.42 percent from 6.12 percent, to take effect from July 28, bank dealers said on Thursday.
"The central bank advised us that it will set its main interest rate at 5.42 percent annually from Monday," a commercial bank dealer told Reuters.
BNB officials were not immediately available for comment.

Interest rates have been steadily falling since March when Bulgaria sealed a $657 million reform and funding package with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and financial markets began to stabilise.
The main rate stood at 18 percent monthly in March following a sharp lev fall to 3,000 to the dollar in February amid political instability.
Under the agreement with the IMF Bulgaria introduced a restrictive fixed exchange rate regime, known as currency board, to restore confidence in the financial system and its lev currency.
Under the mechanism the lev was pegged at 1,000 to the mark as anchor currency.
